title: Trading with customers
summary: Not every sale in TCG Card Shop Simulator is a shelf purchase: the game defines a card trading screen and tracks what a customer is doing with its own set of states.
body: Trading is its own interface in the game, so a trade is a different kind of sale from a customer picking something off a shelf.
Customers have tracked states, which is why the shop can react to a customer who is browsing, waiting or leaving rather than treating them as a single behaviour.
A trade is kept as a record of its own. It holds whether the customer is trading and the last price quoted to them, which is how a negotiation can be picked up again rather than restarted.
The table has two sides. The record keeps the card on the left and the card on the right, so a trade is stored as two positions rather than as a loose pair of cards.
Because trading happens at a screen, keeping a counter free matters when a customer wants to trade rather than buy.
What this entry does not tell you: how often customers offer trades, what they will accept, or how much profit a trade makes. We have not verified those numbers, so we do not print them.

facts.claim: Trading with a customer has its own screen in the game.
The build names a group of its own for changing money at the counter.
Customer behaviour is tracked as a set of states.
Cards handled in trade are the same card objects as elsewhere in the shop.
A customer's trade record holds whether they are trading and the last price quoted to them.
It holds the two cards on the table, one on the left and one on the right.
